# dsh-pricing

DeepSeek peak hours, live token prices and the real spend of every chat — right in
the DSH session h
eader, plus a full spending analytics page.

The chip answers one question: **is it expensive right now, and until when**. It
is shown only for t

he official DeepSeek provider; other providers and local models
get no chip at all.

## Screenshots
## What you get

- **Header chip** — the actual spend of the current session only (`● сессия $1.60`).
During peak hou

rs it turns red and adds `ПИК` plus the end time; the chip label
stays in the plugin language.
- **H

over card** — the provider's peak schedule in its own zone and in yours, the
time left, a four-row p

rice table (peak and off-peak for both models: input,
cache hit, output), the session spend with a t

oken breakdown, an inherited-fork
note and a «Refresh now» action.
- **Settings** — interface langua

ge: Russian, English, Chinese or «Auto» (the
application language). Stored in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\dsh-pr

icing\settings.json`.
- **Spending page** — a sidebar section with periods, charts, session tables,
per-session details and CSV export.
## Languages

Strings live in `client.js` (`STRINGS.ru|en|zh`), plugin-list titles in
`locale/*.json`. The languag

e is switched in **Plugins → dsh-pricing** and written
to the same settings file. Precedence: the st

ored setting (`ru`, `en`, `zh`) →
`auto`, which follows `document.documentElement.lang` / `navigator

.language` →
the default `ru`.
## Where prices come from

`https://api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/pricing.md` — the docs page is available
as markdown, so
it is parsed without an HTML parser.
The host half:

- fetches the page every `refreshHours` (6 by default) and parses the `PRICING`
table and the `Peak

hours are …` sentence;
- **validates** the result: all three metrics for both models, `peak ≥ off >

in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\dsh-pricing\prices.json`;
- serves it over loopback `127.0.0.1:49237` (`/state`,
APPDATA%\dsh-pricing\plugin.log`.

`data/pricing.json` ships as a reference snapshot, so the plugin works offline and
on the very first

on the very first start.
## Session spend

The provider returns tokens, not money. Spend is therefore computed **from the
actual tokens in the

durable session log**: every `assistant/message` and
`compaction/summary` record with `usage` (uncac

hed input, cache reads, cache
writes, output) is priced with the tariff **in force at that record's

own
timestamp** — peak or off-peak. Old peak turns stay priced at the peak rate even
when the curren
t period is off-peak.

Parsed logs are cached by path/size/mtime, so polling never re-reads an unchanged
file. The chip sho

ws the session cost; the card shows the same number with a token
breakdown.
## Reset point

The card has two slices: **Session** (the whole chat) and **Since the last reset**
(only what accumu
lated after pressing «Reset»).

- «Reset» stores the moment (and the request number it happened at) for the current
session; the sec

ond counter starts from there.
- The total is never erased: «Session» stays complete.
- The chip alw

ays shows the reset slice: before any reset it equals the whole chat.
- «Clear reset» removes the ma

rker, both slices align again.
- Resets are per chat, stored in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\dsh-pricing\resets.j

son` and
survive restarts.
## Time zones

Peak windows are stored in the publishing zone (`peak.tz`, currently `UTC`),
compared as absolute in

stants through `Intl`, and displayed in your local zone.
DeepSeek peaks: `01:00–04:00` and `06:00–10

:00 UTC`, Monday to Friday, excluding
Chinese public holidays; for UTC+5 that is `06:00–09:00` and `

day to Friday, excluding
Chinese public holidays; for UTC+5 that is `06:00–09:00` and `11:00–15:00`.

Holidays are a list of ISO dates in `peak.holidays` (empty by default: the provider
publishes no mac
hine-readable calendar, dates are added by hand).
## Spending page
The **Spending** section in the sidebar is a dedicated page:

- **Overview** — period presets (calendar week default, month, 30 days, a single
day, a custom range

or all time, sorted by cost, with lifetime,
cost, requests, active days and tokens; loaded 100 at a

time.
- **Custom range** — one Monday-first calendar: first click sets the start, second
sets the en

d; clicking another date starts a new range.
- **Time zone selector** — affects grouping only: each

request is priced by its own
instant, so the same date in different zones yields different request s

ets.
- **Charts** — days for any period; for a single selected day the chart switches to
hours (0–23

). Hovering a bar shows its date, sum and request count immediately.
- **Toolbar** — «Refresh» rebui

lds the index, the last build time is shown next to
it, «Reset view» returns to the default view.
-

**Navigation** — breadcrumbs with a back stack (up to 20 steps) and ‹ › arrows for
day/week/month.
-

**Session detail** — the whole lifetime of one session, its days, hours and an
«Open session» butto

n.
- **CSV** — export of the selected period or session.

The host keeps an index in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\dsh-pricing\analytics.json`: per log the
size, mtime and

a compact record list. Only changed logs are reparsed; the build

## Limitations

- Search and Fetch API calls are billed per request ($0.75 per 1,000), not per
token, so they are no

t part of the token spend.
- Deleted session logs cannot be priced; only logs on disk are counted.
-

If the provider changes the page markup, the snapshot is not applied and the
plugin keeps the last

verified prices (the failure goes to the log).
- Chinese public holidays are manual: add ISO dates t
o `peak.holidays` when needed.
